correctness.rationale: Periodic rotor states on a path are exactly rooted orientations; necessity follows from last departures, sufficiency from explicit directed Euler tour. Successive marked-rotor excursions return to 0 in 2i steps except the final arrival, establishing first-entry formula for every n and subset. Conditioning on the largest mark yields the polynomial. Strict coordinate monotonicity proves extremizers. The weighted Bernoulli sum plus bounded farthest mark proves mean and CLT. All independent embedded checks replay from package bytes.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest comparable general statements bound exploration time or compute phases. Even their explicit full-graph algorithms do not provide the closed clock polynomial indexed by arbitrary endpoint rotor subsets, unique conditional extrema, mean, or Gaussian limit. The exact (n−1)^2 cover time is a different statistic: the all-right state enters its Euler-tour orbit at (n−2)^2 before the far endpoint is first visited at (n−1)^2.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The recurrence clock is the first entrance into the FULL state orbit (position plus all rotors), not first vertex coverage or first return to launch. Cyclic and path walks are not equivalent under boundary conditions: deleting an edge creates two degree-one ends and changes the state space. The general phase simulation makes the observable computable for any given initial rotor state but does not state or trivially specialize to the claimed exact distribution and fluctuation law.

value.rationale: First full-state periodic entry is a canonical operational quantity of rotor-walk graph exploration. The exact clock polynomial simultaneously resolves every finite-time population for all path lengths, sharp worst-case and fixed-rotor-count extremizers, exact expected initialization delay, and universal m^(3/2) Gaussian fluctuations. Unlike a single n-specific census or worst-case bound, the result characterizes the entire initialization ensemble.
